_comment: Ceilings for the context budget, checked by scripts/context_budget.py --check (CI job lint). Policy: ceiling = observed value + ~5% headroom, so CI catches regressions without flagging noise. After a deliberate slimming, tighten to the new observed values + ~5%; raise a ceiling only together with the change that justifies the growth. Values are BYTES of the text a tool renders to the model - the value of a frontmatter field, not the `key: "value"` entry carrying it, and the first body paragraph where a command or agent declares no description; the script converts them to calibrated cl100k estimates for the report (see BYTES_PER_TOKEN there). agents_md_bytes, descriptor_bytes, command_bytes and agent_bytes are the startup surface - paid on every session of the edition whether or not any of it is used, which makes a rarely-invoked skill or agent expensive rather than cheap. command_bytes and agent_bytes are measured on the .claude tree, the richest of the three tool surfaces: Cursor's equivalents differ slightly and Codex has no commands or agents directory at all, so for a Codex session those two categories over-state the cost by their whole value. body_bytes is the per-invocation cost of skill bodies, an order of magnitude above the startup surface, which is why it is gated rather than left unmeasured. Current values: python3 scripts/context_budget.py.
